evidence_level: Quasi-experimental retrospective comparison (national PNSB panel data 2000-2010 restricted to 64 COPASA-only and 256 municipal-only Brazilian localities, non-parametric Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon tests) plus 15 semi-structured sector-specialist interviews. ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, non-random management-model assignment and no control for confounding municipal characteristics are acknowledged limitations.
institutional_context: COPASA's 2006 IPO (initial public offering) on the São Paulo Stock Exchange; state legislation and decrees governing water/sanitation concessions; ARSAE (state sanitation regulatory agency) oversight

evidence_level: Qualitative ethnographic case study (single South African region, one year of fieldwork). JBI qualitative-checklist rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, sustained direct fieldwork strengthens credibility despite single-region scope.
institutional_context: Private water use on game farms and nature reserves is conceived and managed as a private commodity deriving from land ownership, largely exempted from state water regulation, while the nearby town of Vaalwater and township of Leseding experience unmet minimum water-provision standards

evidence_level: Qualitative multi-site interview study (37 informants across 11 US municipal water utilities, systematic hybrid inductive-deductive coding, IRB-reviewed). JBI qualitative-checklist rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, matched focal-city/comparison-city design across 2 states strengthens comparative credibility.
institutional_context: Utility-level rate-setting, shutoff, and customer-assistance-program (CAP) policy discretion exercised by utility managers, staff and elected officials; Safe Drinking Water Act compliance mandates set water-quality cost floors

evidence_level: Qualitative case study (single Delhi informal settlement, on-site interviews and questionnaire survey over several months). JBI qualitative-checklist rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, single-settlement scope limits generalizability but direct fieldwork and specific legal-status documentation strengthen internal credibility.
institutional_context: Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act 1956, Section 3 notification determining a settlement's formal legal status; Constitution of India Article 21 (right to life, judicially interpreted in 2002 by the Supreme Court to include the right to safe drinking water); notified-slum residents receive water access on exceptional/discretionary grounds rather than as regular DJB customers with enforceable rights

evidence_level: Qualitative multi-site interview study (12 of 29 invited stakeholders across 5 US West Coast cities, with a member-checking validation workshop). JBI qualitative-checklist rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, authors explicitly flag the small, non-representative sample as a limitation of this emergent-topic scoping study.
institutional_context: Access to WASH (water, sanitation, hygiene) services for people experiencing homelessness is contingent on ad hoc government/nonprofit funding arrangements and local permitting processes rather than an established entitlement; housing status is decoupled from access to the underlying WASH infrastructure ('dwelling paradox')

evidence_level: Narrative/scoping review with a documented systematic search strategy (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, no date/language restriction) synthesizing primary-study and case-example evidence across multiple high-income countries. AMSTAR 2 rating deferred pending the official instrument and full appendix search strategy; provisional confidence: moderate, breadth of independently-sourced case examples (USA, France, Slovakia, Australia) across the same racial/administrative-exclusion mechanism strengthens the synthesis, tempered by reliance on secondary case selection rather than a fully reproducible systematic review methodology in the visible text.
legal_context: mixed (common law and civil law jurisdictions surveyed)
institutional_context: Systematic review/synthesis of administrative and legal exclusion mechanisms across high-income countries: racial municipal underbounding (exclusion from incorporation/annexation), property-ownership-linked service eligibility, full-cost-pricing tariff models, and criminalization of open defecation/urination for people without stable housing

evidence_level: Qualitative ethnographic case study (single Roma settlement, eastern Slovakia, fieldwork 1999-2014). JBI qualitative-checklist rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, sustained 15-year direct ethnographic engagement strengthens credibility despite single-settlement scope.
institutional_context: Unclear/disputed land ownership status (nejasné vlastnícke vzťahy) of the Roma settlement precluding extension of the standard municipal water network; municipal council discretion over infrastructure investment decisions; fixed quarterly water fee charged despite no household water meters installed

evidence_level: Qualitative multi-level case study (holistic regime analysis across a Bolivian metropolitan region plus embedded extreme-case studies, 4 fieldwork periods 2012-2020, methods triangulation across narrative/formally-arranged/semi-structured interviews). JBI qualitative-checklist rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, real regime-coverage data (Table 4) strengthens the holistic-case component, though embedded cases are purposively selected extreme cases by design. NOTE: this thesis's Paper II duplicates study S410's findings and was not double-counted in this record's extraction -- see extraction_database.csv extraction_note.
institutional_context: Three co-existing water/sanitation governance regimes analysed via a 6-characteristic institutionalisation framework (infrastructure, actors and organisation mode, social coordination, rational values, financing, legislation): a municipal regime (formal municipal enterprises), a community regime (600+ CBOs of varying legal-entity status -- OTBs, which are part of the political-administrative system but are not themselves legal entities; service cooperatives, legally registered entities with specific administrative compliance requirements; and informal water committees with no legal governance requirements), and an individual regime (unregulated self-supply via tanker trucks and on-site systems)

evidence_level: Mixed-methods case study (3 Kenyan sub-county sites, 80 stakeholder interviews plus a full 12-month police-occurrence-book conflict log and the independently-compiled ACLED database). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, triangulation across interview, documentary, and independent conflict-database sources strengthens credibility despite the 3-site scope.
legal_context: common law with parallel indigenous customary institutions
institutional_context: Kenya's Water Act 2002 (revised 2016) establishing WRUAs as the lowest statutory level of water-resource management, responsible for user registration, catchment management plans, extraction monitoring, by-law enforcement, and conflict resolution, operating alongside indigenous Maasai institutions (Olosho elders' councils regulating grazing/water-point access and imposing fines; Laibon spiritual authority over forest/water-tower resources)

evidence_level: Cross-national descriptive survey (48 Asia-Pacific countries, secondary-data compilation, explicitly labelled 'preliminary observations' by the OECD authors). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate -- near-comprehensive regional coverage is a strength, but reliance on secondary per-country data of uneven quality/completeness and a purely descriptive cross-tabulation (no controlled analysis) are real limitations the authors themselves flag.
legal_context: mixed (48 jurisdictions of varying legal systems)
institutional_context: Cross-national survey (OECD Water Governance Indicator Framework, 12 principles) assessing each country's water law/policy framework, regulatory-body mandate clarity, financing instruments (abstraction and pollution charges), integrity/anti-corruption mechanisms, stakeholder engagement, and monitoring/evaluation (key performance indicators) against the OECD Principles on Water Governance

evidence_level: Cross-sectional mixed-methods survey (385 households, Mavoko Municipality, Kenya). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, calculated sample size and structured questionnaire support the low policy-compliance findings, though single-municipality scope limits generalisation.
institutional_context: Kenya's Environment, Sanitation and Health Policy plus land/housing planning regulations and building codes, whose implementation is assessed via household policy-awareness and compliance rates in a municipality with an 86% deficit in sewerage-treatment capacity and a sewer network covering <1% of its jurisdiction

evidence_level: Qualitative comparative case study (58 focus groups, 24 KIIs, 3 feedback meetings, 7 Ugandan towns). JBI qualitative-checklist rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, triangulation across FGD/KII/feedback-meeting sources strengthens credibility despite non-random town selection.
legal_context: common law with legal pluralism (informal norms)
institutional_context: Uganda's decentralised local-government system, analysed through legal pluralism: formal permit regimes (housing permits, water permits/boreholes, street-vending permits) applied with variable, often lax, enforcement by local officials, alongside informal norms and elite/patronage capture

evidence_level: Qualitative documental/literature synthesis (Brazilian national sanitation-participation policy). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, no direct fieldwork or primary sample, relies on secondary documental sources.
institutional_context: Brazil's National Policy for Basic Sanitation (Politica Nacional de Saneamento Basico, Law 11.445/2007), which established universal access and popular/social participation as founding principles, creating participative social-control arenas (e.g. municipal sanitation councils) whose efficacy depends on governments' willingness to be controlled

evidence_level: Cross-sectional survey with GIS analysis (341 stratified-random-sampled settlements, Jaffna, Sri Lanka), plus focus groups/interviews. MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, stratified random sampling and direct site observation strengthen the toilet-facility/building-code findings.
legal_context: mixed (common law with customary/administrative land tenure practices)
institutional_context: Sri Lankan building/planning regulations requiring formal permits for house construction (including minimum toilet/bathroom dimensions); the majority of underserved settlements (USSs) do not obtain building permission because residents hold less than the minimum land allotment, occupy land reservations, or lack legal land tenure

evidence_level: Systematic scoping review (first review addressing the transitional-displacement WASH evidence gap). AMSTAR2 rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, systematic multi-database search strengthens credibility, though scoping reviews do not formally exclude on primary-study quality.
institutional_context: Systematic scoping review of environmental health, including WASH access, among forcibly displaced populations in the 'transitional' stage between the emergency phase and durable solutions, encompassing gaps in legal status/documentation, humanitarian governance and host-state service provision during this under-studied phase of displacement

evidence_level: Cross-sectional household survey (3,947 migrant households, 30 randomly selected slum settlements, Ludhiana, India). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, large sample and random settlement selection stratified by legal notification status.
institutional_context: India's slum 'notification' system, under which slums are formally designated ('notified') or not ('non-notified') by the municipal/state government, with notified status conferring greater eligibility for civic-amenity provision and documentation (ration cards, voter cards) than non-notified or open-space settlement

evidence_level: Narrative review synthesis (African correctional-facility menstrual-hygiene literature). AMSTAR2 rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, narrative rather than fully systematic synthesis methodology across heterogeneous African jurisdictions.
institutional_context: Absence of gender-responsive prison policies and inconsistent implementation of global standards such as the UN Bangkok Rules governing the treatment of women prisoners, examined through a narrative synthesis of barriers to menstrual hygiene management (a specific dimension of institutional WASH access) in African correctional services

evidence_level: Narrative critical review (Nigeria SDG 6 progress, 2016-2024, secondary national/international data sources). AMSTAR2 rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, secondary-source review without a fully systematic search protocol reported.
institutional_context: Qualitative critical review of Nigeria's SDG 6 governance framework, assessing governance inefficiencies (bureaucratic delays, weak regulatory enforcement), policy-enforcement gaps, and infrastructure-investment shortfalls against secondary data from national and international sources (Federal Ministry of Water Resources, National Bureau of Statistics, UN, WHO, UNICEF, World Bank)

evidence_level: Qualitative case study (interviews, observation, documentation, 9 of 39 sections, Bambili, Cameroon). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, direct interviews with BWA personnel and community leaders strengthen the governance-capture findings despite single-community scope.
legal_context: mixed (statutory law with customary/traditional chieftaincy authority)
institutional_context: The BWA's own constitution formally requires an annual General Assembly vote (headed by the village chief) to elect the Board of Directors, but in practice the chief directly appoints board members via 'extraordinary meetings', bypassing the constitutionally mandated democratic election process and capturing decision-making power over rural water-supply governance

evidence_level: Cross-sectional survey with stated-preference discrete-choice experiment (1,167 households, 30 clusters, Kigali, Rwanda). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, large geographically dispersed sample and formal WTP methodology.
institutional_context: Kigali lacks a centralised sewer system and regulates on-site sanitation via local administrative cell-level government units; manual pit emptying and illegal dumping of faecal sludge carry a stiff fine under municipal regulation, but enforcement is imperfect, and this analysis quantifies household willingness-to-pay (WTP) against the cost of regulated/improved emptying services

evidence_level: Qualitative ethnographic case study (6 months fieldwork, 50 semi-structured interviews, Hyderabad, India). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, sustained direct fieldwork and multi-stakeholder interviews strengthen credibility despite single-settlement scope.
institutional_context: Uneven municipal governance of water, sanitation and environmental infrastructure in an informal settlement, in which formal municipal provision is contaminated/unreliable, shifting the burden of coping (private tankers, groundwater extraction, NGO/health-camp reliance) onto residents, particularly women, with fragmented and non-structural institutional response

evidence_level: Cross-sectional observational study with instrumental-variable identification (142,838 households, multi-country Africa). ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, very large sample and IV design support a causal interpretation despite self-reported outcome measures.
institutional_context: Presence of active vs. inactive (closed) mining sites used as a spatial exposure, combined with an instrumental-variable design and an explicit test of the moderating role of local governance and institutional strength on the water-security, health and economic effects of household proximity to mining

evidence_level: Panel/longitudinal observational study (176 California water districts, 3 election cycles, 2009-2020). ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: high, near-universal sample of qualifying districts and administrative (not self-reported) election/performance records.
institutional_context: Elected water-district board governance under California special-district law; boards are elected at regular multi-year cycles, but seats frequently go uncontested (unopposed incumbents), and the paper analyses statutory/jurisdictional fragmentation (municipal overlap) as a driver of uncontested elections and elections' consequences for discretionary/redistributive policy (low-income bill assistance) versus heavily regulated compliance (Safe Drinking Water Act water-quality violations)

evidence_level: Qualitative Community Capitals Framework literature synthesis (Mexico, national). AMSTAR2 rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, secondary-source synthesis with selection of cited literature not fully systematic.
institutional_context: Community Capitals Framework (financial, built, natural, political, cultural, human, social capital) applied to Mexico's sanitation governance, examining how absence of social cohesion, unreliable government policies/strategies, corruption entrenched in political capital, and lack of appropriation of implemented strategies drive wasted resources and persistently low sanitation coverage, particularly in poorer states lacking an adequate political framework

evidence_level: Mixed-methods DPSIR study (413 household surveys, 5 municipalities, Paraiba, Brazil, 2021 and 2024). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, primary survey data cross-validated with secondary reservoir/economic indicators, though 5 purposively selected municipalities limit national generalisation.
institutional_context: Driving force-Pressure-State-Impact-Response (DPSIR) governance-analysis framework applied to a large-scale federal water-transposition infrastructure investment (PISF) whose centralised planning and management, the paper argues, has produced cost overruns and inadequate management, disconnected from continuous household-level water delivery despite the infrastructure investment

evidence_level: Systematic review (household coping with unreliable water supply, multi-country). AMSTAR2 rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, systematic multi-database search across a heterogeneous set of underlying primary studies.
institutional_context: Systematic review of household coping strategies in response to unreliable/intermittent water supply, examining how income, education, land tenure, and the regulatory environment for poor and vulnerable consumers influence which coping strategies (illegal connections, storage, alternative sources, vending) households adopt

evidence_level: Cross-sectional observational study with OLS/logit regression (307 villages, national China survey). ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, national survey-linked dataset but authors themselves flag a limited sample-size constraint.
institutional_context: China's rural infrastructure planning regulations set guidelines for coverage by population size/density, but implementation depends on the primary funder of each infrastructure type (village self-financing vs. higher-level government transfer) and the status of local village governance, both formally tested as explanatory variables for unequal infrastructure availability

evidence_level: Narrative/systematic literature review (US drinking-water regulation, national). AMSTAR2 rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, broad review without a single reported systematic search protocol.
institutional_context: US federal drinking-water regulatory framework (EPA standards under the Safe Drinking Water Act, including the Lead and Copper Rule) reviewed via a socioecological lens across the life course, examining how regulation, infrastructure and policy shape variation in drinking-water safety, access and consumption by age and race/ethnicity

evidence_level: Qualitative political-ecology case study (Hanoi, Vietnam). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, relies on secondary policy documents and historical infrastructure records rather than primary fieldwork.
institutional_context: Multilevel water governance in Hanoi, combining a results-based national target programme (NTP3) with regulated tariff calculation based on water meters, consumer contracts, and identification of illegal connections; tariffs are monitored and periodically reviewed by each district's People's Committee, producing district-to-district tariff variation, within a broader context of foreign investment and private-sector participation (PSP) in urban water infrastructure

evidence_level: Mixed-methods study (FGDs, KIIs, document review, 3 Kenyan counties). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, triangulation across qualitative and coverage-statistic sources, though 3 purposively selected counties limit national generalisation.
institutional_context: Kenya's 2010 constitutional recognition of water/sanitation as a fundamental human right, and subsequent sector reforms devolving water/sanitation responsibility to county governments, assessed against continued weak governance, inadequate financing and socio-cultural/environmental barriers

evidence_level: Cross-sectional survey with PLS structural equation modelling (416 informal dwellers, 3 tenure-status groups, Doornkop, South Africa). ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, stratified random sampling and formal SEM validation, single-settlement scope.
institutional_context: Post-1996 South African constitutional right to sufficient water and sanitation (Government of South Africa 1996) implemented via traditional water management/governance, assessed through UNESCO 'human dignity' and 'human equality' water-governance principles across three tenure-status groups (relocated, tenure-allocated, squatter) within one informal settlement

evidence_level: Qualitative documentary/policy analysis (London public-toilet governance, UK). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, secondary closure statistics from named public-health/press sources support the documentary analysis.
institutional_context: Absence of any statutory legal requirement for UK local authorities to provide public toilets, combined with central-government austerity budget cuts, resulting in fragmented, reactive governance responsibility for public sanitation and no dedicated public-toilet policies or budgets in most cities

evidence_level: Repeated cross-sectional national administrative-census study with binomial logistic regression (tens of thousands of Brazilian rural elementary schools, 2011 vs 2023). ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: high, national administrative School Census microdata with multivariable adjustment, though self-declared by school directors without independent audit.
institutional_context: Absence of a coordinated national policy specifically for WASH-in-schools in Brazil; existing complementary programmes (Funasa's 2005 Agua na Escola programme, which reached only 606 of 889 planned schools by 2009; the Ministry of Education's PDDE per-student funding formula and PAR planning instrument) are poorly inter-sectorally articulated, and the PDDE's enrolment-based funding formula is argued in the discussion to structurally disadvantage small, dispersed rural schools' capacity to invest in WASH infrastructure

evidence_level: Qualitative narrative analysis of local-government reform documentation (New Zealand, national). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, relies on local-government narrative/documentary sources for a national-scale institutional reform.
institutional_context: New Zealand's Three Waters Reform, a major legislative and institutional restructuring that shifted water-service-delivery control from 67 local councils to 4 regional Water Services Entities in response to the 2016 Havelock North water-contamination crisis, intended to improve efficiency, infrastructure investment and regulatory oversight; analysed via local-government narratives of the reform's implementation

evidence_level: Qualitative intraurban comparative case study (Cape Town sewerage governance, South Africa). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, comparative intraurban design strengthens the heterogeneity findings despite single-city scope.
institutional_context: Governance of heterogeneous sewerage infrastructure configurations in Cape Town, combining networked (piped sewer) and non-networked (e.g. pit latrines, chemical toilets, communal ablution blocks) technologies operated by a mix of municipal, private and community actors, moving beyond a norm of uniform networked provision

evidence_level: Panel-data regression study (Brazilian municipalities directly providing WWS, fixed/random/correlated-random-effects specifications). ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: high, near-comprehensive municipal panel with formal Mundlak-test model selection, though mixed/non-robust significance across specifications for some dimensions.
institutional_context: Intermunicipal cooperation (IMC) as a formal local-government-adopted governance arrangement for water/wastewater services, distinguishing participation in IMC per se from the cumulative duration of that cooperation as separate explanatory legal/institutional variables

evidence_level: Mixed-methods case study (key informant interviews, field observation and measurement, GIS/hydraulic modelling, 4 Ethiopian cities). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, combination of primary field-measured data and secondary utility records across 4 purposively selected cities.
institutional_context: Institutional and governance complexities of urban drinking-water systems (UDWS) in Ethiopia, including ineffective policies and weak institutions, examined alongside technical/environmental complexities (non-revenue water, distribution-network pressure imbalances) across four major cities

evidence_level: Cross-national observational study (DAUSR determinants, multi-country secondary data). ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, relies on national-level secondary mortality/sanitation-coverage statistics rather than a harmonised primary dataset.
institutional_context: Cross-national analysis of sanitation-governance gaps as a driver of Deaths Attributable to Unsafe Sanitation in Rural areas (DAUSRs), examining how demographic ageing interacts with weak sanitation governance and infrastructure strategies across several countries including China, Brazil, India, Kenya and Bangladesh

evidence_level: Qualitative comparative political-economy case study (multiple cities, CWIS/CBS sectoral-regime analysis). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, multi-city comparison strengthens the regime-fragmentation findings despite non-random city selection.
institutional_context: Political economy and socio-technical sectoral-regime analysis of citywide inclusive sanitation (CWIS) policy, examining how container-based sanitation (CBS) enterprises interact with fragmented formal/informal governance regimes (sewered networks, septic tanks, CBS) and city-level planning/policy processes

evidence_level: Cross-sectional survey with formal significance testing (129 Grade 7 learners, 5 primary schools, eThekwini, South Africa). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, validated WHO WASH-in-Schools instrument with 72% response rate, single-district scope.
institutional_context: Cross-sectional assessment of WASH interventions in schools against the WHO Surveillance of WASH in Schools Tool, discussed in relation to national policy commitments (SDG 6 and South African school-health policy) and the institutional capacity, governance, monitoring and accountability mechanisms needed to sustain school WASH systems

evidence_level: Comparative mixed-methods study structured by the Human Right to Sanitation framework (informal vs. formal settlements, Nairobi, Kenya). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, structured comparison against a validated rights framework, purposively selected settlement pairs.
institutional_context: Comparative analysis of sanitation access through the lens of the Human Right to Sanitation (HRtS) framework -- availability, accessibility, quality/safety, acceptability, affordability -- across informal and formal settlement types in Nairobi, examining how differential legal/tenure status underlying settlement formality shapes lived sanitation experience against each HRtS dimension

evidence_level: Cross-sectional perception survey validated against historical climate data (206 respondents across 3 Nepalese districts, 30 years of climate data). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, formal sample-size calculation and independent climate-data cross-validation.
legal_context: mixed (statutory law with community-based water/sanitation user-committee governance)
institutional_context: Community-managed WASH governance model, in which Water Users and Sanitation Committees (WUSCs) and caretakers hold institutional responsibility for system sustainability, assessed for resilience to climate-change impacts (water-source depletion, seasonal turbidity, floods/landslides, droughts) across three physiographic regions

evidence_level: Historical documentary/archival case study (early-1900s US colonial Philippines). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, relies on historical colonial-era policy documents and records, not a contemporary sampled population.
institutional_context: Early-1900s US colonial sanitary law and enforcement apparatus in the Philippines, including sanitary regulations empowering inspectors to invade the rights of homes and enforce compliance with sanitary laws, cholera-pass systems regulating movement, and a Philippine Legislature law banning the use of night soil, deployed alongside dam, water-supply-network and irrigation infrastructure investment

evidence_level: Qualitative case study with theoretical framework (Detroit water-affordability crisis, USA). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, relies on documentary/secondary financial-record sources for a single-city case study.
institutional_context: Municipal wastewater/stormwater ratepayer financing structure, whose politically and economically uneven management -- compounded by the need to comply with state water-quality regulations -- is argued to have produced a racialized water-affordability crisis in majority-Black Detroit; the city also used residential water shutoffs (disconnections) as a revenue-collection strategy

evidence_level: Documentary/media-report analysis with an embedded 8-household qualitative case analysis (Portugal, national). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, national disconnection statistics are broadly representative though partly media-report-derived; the 8-household deep-dive is a small non-random sample.
institutional_context: Portugal does not have an explicit recognition of the Human Right to Water and Sanitation (HRtWS) in its domestic legal framework, despite voting in favour at the UN General Assembly (Resolution 64/292) and being party to the ICESCR; water-service disconnection for payment default is legally possible and was used at scale during the 2010-2013 Eurozone economic-crisis austerity period

evidence_level: Qualitative policy-document analysis using an original evaluative framework (Indian Himalayan Region, multi-state). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, systematic review of named national/state policy documents via an original but not independently validated matrix (PHIM).
institutional_context: Comparative policy analysis of India's National Water Policy (2002, revised 2012), Jal Shakti Abhiyan (2019), the Composite Water Management Index, and state-level policy (e.g. Uttarakhand State Action Plan on Climate Change) against Heritage Water Architecture (HWA, e.g. naulaas, dhaaras, baodis) governance, using an original Policy-Heritage Integration Matrix (PHIM) to evaluate governance gaps and institutional-coordination failures between modern piped-water policy and traditional systems

evidence_level: Single in-depth qualitative case study (Pucara, Peru). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, single-community case study using an original, not independently validated, sustainability-assessment method.
institutional_context: Integral community management model for renewable-energy-based sanitation services, formally evaluated across five sustainability dimensions -- technical, economic, social/ethical, environmental, and institutional/organisational -- with the institutional/organisational dimension identified as especially complex and critical to project sustainability

evidence_level: Qualitative case study (Nyayo Highrise estate, Nairobi, Kenya). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, single-estate case study relying on qualitative fieldwork/interview-based analysis.
institutional_context: Recent Kenyan water-sector reforms emphasising water governance over technological network expansion, examined through variegated 'technopolitics' of water-pressure management by different urban actors -- manipulation of the pipe network, decentralized technology provision, and resident activism/protest -- in one middle-class housing estate suffering extreme water shortages despite unrestricted access historically enjoyed by other parts of the city since the colonial period

evidence_level: Qualitative case study with embedded quantitative water-demand estimation (12 interviews, 4 boreholes, Chitungwiza, Zimbabwe). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, direct interviews during an acute crisis period, small purposive sample.
institutional_context: Municipal water governance in an under-resourced Zimbabwean city, examined for its capacity to meet WHO 'Safe Hands' handwashing water-demand guidance during COVID-19, highlighting institutional bottlenecks, inadequate financial resources, and lack of inter- and intra-governmental coordination within and between central and local governments across sectors as structural constraints on municipal water planning and governance response capacity

evidence_level: Simulation/decision-analytic modelling study (2 disaggregated service areas, Federal District of Brazil, multiobjective optimization across future scenarios). ROBINS-I rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, formal disaggregated simulation methodology, though model-based rather than directly observed household outcomes.
institutional_context: Deeply uncertain infrastructure-investment pathway planning applying multiobjective optimization and disaggregated service-area-level performance/vulnerability assessment across time, explicitly incorporating historical socioeconomic inequity and differences in service-area governance/investment history as structural drivers of unequal vulnerability to future hydroclimatic and socioeconomic scenarios

evidence_level: Mixed-methods study with formal sanitary inspection (384 households, 2 transfer stations, 1 treatment facility, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate-high, combination of household survey, direct risk assessment and standardised sanitary-inspection instrument.
institutional_context: Ethiopia's Sanitation and Faecal Sludge Management (FSM) policy, aligned with SDG targets for 2030 and aiming to improve sanitation access and promote safe fecal-sludge practices, assessed against actual sanitary-inspection compliance at fecal-sludge-management transfer stations and treatment/disposal facilities

evidence_level: Mixed-methods forensic case study (Pressure-and-Release framework, semi-structured interviews plus quantitative drought/electricity/tanker-delivery data, Qwaqwa, South Africa). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: high, precise quantitative service-delivery data (1,500/5,000 tankers) triangulated with qualitative interviews.
institutional_context: Forensic Pressure-and-Release framework analysis of drought-response governance in Qwaqwa, identifying apartheid-era spatial/infrastructure inequalities, corruption, and contemporary institutional mismanagement (severely under-delivered emergency water-tanker response) as compounding factors that aggravated the impacts of a genuinely severe 2015-2020 precipitation deficit combined with national electricity load-shedding

evidence_level: Qualitative governance-framework/institutional-mandate document analysis (Ghana, national). JBI rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: low-moderate, relies on published governance/policy documentation rather than primary fieldwork.
institutional_context: Systematic assessment of gaps in Ghana's water and sanitation governance framework -- institutional mandates, coordination across national and district-level bodies, financing, and regulatory enforcement -- identifying what is structurally missing relative to good-governance benchmarks for achieving universal WASH access

evidence_level: Qualitative comparative policy review citing primary survey evidence (Nigeria, with Ghana/Kenya comparators). AMSTAR2 rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, the review's most specific quantitative evidence derives from a single cited 193-household Makurdi survey, not the review's own primary data collection.
institutional_context: Comparative review of water-governance frameworks across Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya, examining the failure of institutions responsible for water regulation and management, over-regulation of supplies and complex tariff structures, and Kenya's Water Act 2002 (revised 2006) decentralisation reforms shifting regulatory/management capacity to local Water Service Boards, benchmarked against OECD water-governance principles to identify adaptive-capacity mainstreaming pathways toward SDG 6

evidence_level: Cross-sectional household survey with chi-square/correlation significance testing (internally displaced households, Marawi City, Philippines). MMAT rating deferred pending the official instrument; provisional confidence: moderate, formal statistical testing on a structured survey, though sampling frame not fully specified in the retrieved text.

institutional_context: Mixed-methods diagnostic sustainability-check framework (household survey of 100 households per town, water point survey, key-informant interviews with Regional Water Bureau/Town Water Utility staff) applied to 7 small towns' piped water schemes, examining Ethiopia's Town Water Board governance structure established via regional proclamations with limited formal accountability to town administrations, absence of a national/regional urban water regulatory agency, tariff-approval authority resting with town administrations, and the near-total absence (except Wukro) of shared yard-connection provisions allowing low-income households in compound housing to jointly apply for and pay for a water connection

evidence_level: Single-study evidence (mixed-methods social-ecological case study: 2,103-household survey, complete infrastructure audit of 2,805 tubewells, 6 focus groups, 13 key-informant interviews); risk-of-bias rating deferred pending official application of the MMAT (see RISK_OF_BIAS.md and extraction_database.csv risk_of_bias_tool/risk_of_bias_rating for S506).
institutional_context: Mixed-methods social-ecological systems study (2,103 household surveys, water infrastructure audit of 2,805 tubewells and 19 pond sand filters, 6 focus group discussions, 13 key-informant interviews) of governance and institutional risks to drinking water security in a coastal Bangladeshi polder, examining Union Parishad institutional capacity limits for managing complex piped schemes, a failed formal water-vending tariff system that could not recover costs, elite-influenced/nepotistic allocation of public deep tubewells across unions, absence of formal regulation or oversight of the rapidly growing private self-supply tubewell market, and cross-upazila jurisdictional boundary issues that left one union unable to benefit from formal government water arrangements available elsewhere in the polder

evidence_level: Single-study evidence (narrative policy review applying an eight-step policy analysis framework to national policy/strategy documents and secondary JMP/GSS coverage statistics, explicitly not a systematic review with documented search methodology); risk-of-bias rating deferred pending official application of the project's Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework (see RISK_OF_BIAS.md and extraction_database.csv risk_of_bias_tool/risk_of_bias_rating for S507).
institutional_context: Policy review (eight-step policy analysis framework applied to national policy/strategy documents, JMP/GSS coverage data, and published literature) of Ghana's post-MDGs sanitation situation, examining the Local Government Act (Act 462) assigning MMDAs statutory responsibility for sanitation services, the National Environmental Sanitation Policy's designation of sanitation as households' own financial responsibility, a novel 10% sanitation surcharge on property tax piloted in Ga West Municipal Assembly, absence of a national urban sanitation regulatory strategy, and planned creation of a National Sanitation Authority with regulatory/standard-setting powers

evidence_level: Single-study evidence (qualitative case study: semi-structured interviews and focus groups with rural water committee members plus secondary Conagua/CAEV administrative database review); risk-of-bias rating deferred pending official application of the CASP Qualitative Checklist (see RISK_OF_BIAS.md and extraction_database.csv risk_of_bias_tool/risk_of_bias_rating for S508).
institutional_context: Qualitative case study (semi-structured interviews and focus groups with rural water committee members, 2012 fieldwork; review of Conagua's rural-committee database 2009-2013; review of Veracruz's water regulatory framework -- Ley Número 21 de Aguas del Estado de Veracruz-Llave and Ley 72 de Agua y Saneamiento) of community water organizations (organizaciones comunitarias de servicios de agua y saneamiento, OCSAS, locally called patronatos) in Veracruz, Mexico, examining the absence of formal legal recognition for community water organizations in Mexico -- unlike Chile, Ecuador, and several Central American countries where OCSAS have statutory recognition -- the 'municipal exclusivity' legal argument used by authorities to deny community organizations formal recognition, annual/short-term renewal requirements for rural water committees creating institutional instability, and CAEV's direct administration of rural systems in areas where municipal institutional capacity is absent

evidence_level: Single-study evidence (mixed-methods programme evaluation: 2,105-household survey plus a 294-household disability sub-survey, 62 in-depth interviews, and 60 focus group discussions); risk-of-bias rating deferred pending official application of the MMAT (see RISK_OF_BIAS.md and extraction_database.csv risk_of_bias_tool/risk_of_bias_rating for S509).
institutional_context: Mixed-methods operational research (2,105-household survey, individual survey of physically disabled people, 62 in-depth interviews, 60 focus group discussions) assessing equity mainstreaming in the UNICEF SHAWN II WASH programme, examining needs-based and commitment-based LGA selection scoring criteria, community-level selection processes vulnerable to politicization via traditional-leader involvement, WASHCOM member-selection criteria (gender-balance quotas of 40-50%), the Community-Led Total Sanitation (CLTS) no-subsidy approach with hardship-based support criteria for households unable to construct latrines themselves (due to lack or disability of a male household head), and political interference in water-point siting decisions producing skewed distribution

evidence_level: Single-study evidence (mixed-methods comparative household-survey study: 645 peri-urban and 139 rural households, plus national water-policy document review); risk-of-bias rating deferred pending official application of the MMAT (see RISK_OF_BIAS.md and extraction_database.csv risk_of_bias_tool/risk_of_bias_rating for S510).
institutional_context: Mixed-methods household-survey study (645 peri-urban households across 3 informal settlements, 139 rural households across 13 villages) combined with national water-policy document review, examining Malawi's 1995 Water Works Act establishing the legal basis for parastatal water boards to manage urban/peri-urban water supply, the Lilongwe/Blantyre water boards' 2006 partnerships with community-elected Water User Associations to extend service to underserved peri-urban areas, the Ministry of Water and Irrigation Development's rural water-scheme responsibility (delegated at community level to district assemblies, private contractors, water point committees, or NGOs), and the 2005 National Water Policy's equity principles versus its lack of differentiated urban/rural implementation targets
